1.why: The system enforces session-based ownership checks (auth() verifies s.userId === account.id) for all MFA endpoints.

2.why: Verification codes are single-use and time-bound, but the statement claims they work for any user, which is false.

3.why: Old sessions are deleted on new login (sessions.delete(old)), but the statement claims they still work, which is false.

4.why: OTP secrets are encrypted (await encrypt(secret)) and backup codes are encrypted (encrypted: await encrypt(code)).

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues(), a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are never stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (cookies are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., emailOK, phoneOK, and type checks for OTP/recovery codes).

8.why: Contextual output encoding is applied (esc() function in HTML, and JSON responses are properly escaped).

9.why: Redirects are not open; the system uses client-side routing (location.hash) with no arbitrary URL redirects.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in the headers() function.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are never exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (sensitive data is encrypted or hashed).

13.why: Verification codes are single-use (p.used = true) and time-bound (now > p.expires check).

14.why: Rate-limiting is implemented (p.attempts >= 5 locks the pending OTP, and account.failures >= 5 locks recovery codes).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication (new token() on login), and sessions are invalidated on logout (sessions.delete(a.t)).
